title: Linear descent of the explicit Koszul product-fibre construction
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-size-convention], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $A$ a commutative ring acting on $\mathcal O$ through global sections. Assume countable products of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves are exact. Fix a finite list $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in\Gamma(\mathcal S,\mathcal O)$, allowing $r=0$. Use cochain complexes and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $Q_m=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$, in degrees $[-r,0]$, with the transition multiplication by $b_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a cochain complex $M$, set $B(M)=\prod_{m\geq1}(M\otimes Q_m)$, let $s$ use the quotient-tower transitions, and put
$$F(M)^i=B(M)^i\oplus B(M)^{i-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(d_Bx,(1-s)x-d_By).$$
For a chain map $a:M\to N$, use the product of $a\otimes1$ in both summands to define $F(a)$. This assignment preserves chain homotopies and quasi-isomorphisms and induces an additive $A$-linear functor $C:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-linear-functor]. It represents $R\lim_m(M\otimes^L Q_m)$, with the natural coaugmentation $\kappa_M:M\to C(M)$ induced by the degree-zero inclusions $\mathcal O\to Q_m$. The canonical maps $F(0)\cong0$ and $F(M\oplus N)\cong F(M)\oplus F(N)$ identify these coaugmentations and are natural. In particular, the full subcategory on objects for which $\kappa_M$ is invertible is additive, with the inherited $A$-linear Hom modules, and $C(ta)=tC(a)$ for $t\in A$.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; explicit product/fibre and scalar-descent refinement, agent supplied

proof.text: The transitions are chain maps: in each two-term factor $b_j^m b_j=b_j^{m+1}$, and the degree-zero map is the identity. Tensor these maps with the signed total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Each $Q_m$ has zero terms outside $[-r,0]$ and finite direct sums of $\mathcal O$ as terms; for $r=0$ it is $\mathcal O[0]$ with identity transitions. Such terms are flat: tensoring with $\mathcal O^k$ is the finite direct-sum functor, which preserves short exact sequences coordinatewise, by the definition in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, finite free Koszul complexes and duals

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to $Q_m$, bounded above by $0$ and with the flat terms established in Step 1. Then [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], with fixed argument $Q_m$ on the right, shows that $M\mapsto M\otimes Q_m$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms for arbitrary unbounded $M$, and that its localization is $M\mapsto M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_m$. Its naturality in chain maps of the fixed K-flat argument identifies the localized transitions with the stipulated Koszul transitions. No regularity of the $b_j$ or boundedness of $M$ is used.

Put $u_M=1-s_M$. Since $s_M$ is a chain map, $d_F^2(x,y)=(0,u_Md_Bx-d_Bu_Mx)=0$. For a chain map $a$, write $a_B=\prod_m(a\otimes1)$; its compatibility with transitions gives $a_Bu_M=u_Na_B$, so the specified diagonal $F(a)$ is a chain map. Products are characterized by their projections [def-weil-category-product]; checking projections gives $F(1)=1$, $F(ba)=F(b)F(a)$, $F(a+a')=F(a)+F(a')$ and $F(ta)=tF(a)$ for $t\in A$. Here the $A$-action is the given map to global sections, and every tensor and transition map is linear for it.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; agent-supplied strict fibre calculation

proof.text: If $a-a'=dh+hd$, tensor the homotopy with $1_{Q_m}$. On $M^p\otimes Q_m^q$ the two cross terms cancel because $h$ has degree $-1$: their coefficients are $(-1)^{p-1}$ and $(-1)^p$. Thus $h\otimes1$ is a homotopy between $a\otimes1$ and $a'\otimes1$. It commutes with the tower transitions. Let $h_B$ be its product and define $H^i:F(M)^i\to F(N)^{i-1}$ by $H(x,y)=(h_Bx,-h_By)$. Expanding $dH+Hd$ gives first coordinate $(d h_B+h_Bd)x$ and second coordinate $(u_Nh_B-h_Bu_M)x+(d h_B+h_Bd)y$. The $x$ term in the second coordinate vanishes by transition compatibility. Hence $dH+Hd=F(a)-F(a')$, with exactly the minus sign on the second homotopy coordinate.

source.place: Signed total tensor differential; agent-supplied homotopy calculation

proof.text: Suppose $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Step 2 makes every $a\otimes1_{Q_m}$ a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core] in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, using precisely the assumed exact countable products: $Q(B(a))$ is the morphism between derived products induced by a family of isomorphisms, and is therefore invertible (its inverse is the product of the inverses, as checked at each projection). Because the cohomology functors factor through $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $B(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Now apply [lem-pe-roos-coordinates-quasi-iso] with $V=B(M)$, $V'=B(N)$ and endomorphisms $u_M,u_N$. The chain map in that node is exactly the diagonal $F(a)$ of Step 3, with differential $(dx,ux-dy)$; consequently $F(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products; Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit, and mapping-fibre quasi-isomorphism comparison

proof.text: Let $Q$ denote localization from complexes to $D(\mathcal O)$. The functor $QF$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms by Step 5, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1) produces $C$ with $CQ\cong QF$. Complexes and their derived category are additive; the induced derived $A$-linear structure and additivity and $A$-linearity of $Q$ are supplied by [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], applied to the componentwise $A$-action on module sheaves. Every derived object has a representative complex. Apply [lem-pur-additive-localization-descent] to $q=Q$, $U=QF$, $G=C$ and this comparison: it proves additivity of $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-localization-descent] with the same data and $R=A$ to obtain $C(t\alpha)=tC(\alpha)$ for all derived morphisms, including ones represented by fractions rather than chain maps. Together these two conclusions give the $A$-linear functor required by [def-weil-linear-functor].

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; linear refinement: Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Linear.lean, functor_linear_iff; additive descent as stated by the cited node

proof.text: By [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core], $Q(B(M))$ with its actual projections is the product of the $Q(M\otimes Q_m)$ in the derived category. The strict complex $F(M)$ is a model for the mapping fibre of $u_M$: in the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the chain isomorphism to $\operatorname{Cone}(u_M)[-1]$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$, with inverse $(v,w)\mapsto(w,-v)$. Its first projection is $x$. Rotating the cone triangle, with the corresponding sign on the final connecting map, gives a distinguished triangle $QF(M)\to Q B(M)\xrightarrow{Q(1-s_M)}Q B(M)\to QF(M)[1]$. Thus [def-weil-derived-limit] identifies $QF(M)$ as a derived limit of the tower. Step 2 identifies that tower, including its transitions, with $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_m$. This asserts a specified strict model and its triangle, not a functorial cone construction in an arbitrary triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit, and Tag 07KC, lemma-products; explicit cone identification

proof.text: Let $e_M:M\to B(M)$ have components $z\mapsto z\otimes1$ in the degree-zero summand of $Q_m$. These are chain maps because $1$ has degree $0$ and has zero differential. Transitions are identity on this summand, so $u_Me_M=0$. Therefore $\kappa_M(z)=(e_Mz,0)$ is a chain map, and $F(a)\kappa_M=\kappa_Na$ follows at every product projection. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends this transformation from $Q$ to $CQ$ to a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow C$. Its projection to each tower level is the specified inclusion; under Step 7 it is precisely the coaugmentation of this derived-limit model. No claim of uniqueness from the level projections alone is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; coaugmentation refinement using the strict compatible inclusions

proof.text: Tensor distributes over a binary direct sum by the maps induced by its inclusions and projections. Products do likewise: the inverse maps send $((v_m,w_m))_m$ to $((v_m)_m,(w_m)_m)$ and back, as follows from [def-weil-category-product]. Applying these maps to both fibre coordinates yields $F(M\oplus N)\cong F(M)\oplus F(N)$; the maps commute with $d$, $s$, and all chain maps because all their components are the indicated projections and inclusions. Likewise $F(0)=0$. They send $\kappa_{M\oplus N}$ to $\kappa_M\oplus\kappa_N$ and $\kappa_0$ to the map $0\to0$. These identities persist after localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2),(3). Every derived binary biproduct can be computed on representative complexes since $Q$ is additive [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0A0E strict Koszul model; elementary finite-biproduct coordinate refinement

proof.text: The zero object has invertible $\kappa_0$. If $\kappa_M$ and $\kappa_N$ are invertible, Step 9 identifies $\kappa_{M\oplus N}$ with their direct sum, whose inverse is $\kappa_M^{-1}\oplus\kappa_N^{-1}$. Thus the full subcategory on these objects contains zero and binary biproducts. Its Hom groups are the ambient $A$-modules, and composition remains bilinear; the biproduct identities are unchanged because it is full. This proves additivity with the inherited linear structure. The final scalar identity is the one already proved for all derived morphisms in Step 6.

source.place: Tag 0A0E; elementary consequence of the explicit biproduct and coaugmentation identities

tool_uses.why: K-flatness of bounded finite-free Koszul complexes on an arbitrary ringed site; the unit gives no homological-algebra replacement.
Preservation of quasi-isomorphisms and identification of ordinary tensor by a fixed K-flat complex with derived tensor, natural in the fixed argument; a generic ringed-site tool.
Termwise countable products represent derived products under exactness, needed on an arbitrary module-sheaf category; the unit gives no product theorem.
Diagonal quasi-isomorphism comparison for the displayed fibre differential in any abelian category; no pro-etale restriction occurs in this node.
Additivity of the descended functor through the derived additive localization; no unit-specific geometric result replaces this categorical fact.
